The CSO groups immigrants by the country or region they came from, and emigrants by where they went. In the twelve months to April 2026, the largest number of immigrants, 52,200, came from countries outside the EU, the United Kingdom, the United States, Canada and Australia. More people left for Australia than arrived from it, and the same was true of Canada and of the countries that were EU members before 2004.

{{< chart migration-by-place >}}

## Born abroad

At the 2022 census, 20% of people living in Ireland were born outside the country. The share was highest in Dublin, at 25%, followed by Monaghan and Donegal. It was lowest in Kilkenny, Offaly and Tipperary, at about 14%.

{{< chart migration-born-abroad-map >}}

Compared with other EU countries, Ireland has a high share of people born abroad. On 1 January 2025, 23.3% of people living in Ireland were born in another country, the 4th highest share in the EU, after Luxembourg, Malta and Cyprus. The EU average was 14.6%. Eurostat's figure is for 2025, three years after the census.
